description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/lib.rs:152

```rust
pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler;
```

This is the same orphan re-export already flagged by JMAP-3t94.9 for
its positional oddity. The contract-risk angle is separate:

1. **Forever pin to upstream.** A `pub use` of a type from another
   crate pins the major version of the upstream crate into this
   crate's public API. If `jmap-server` cuts a major version that
   changes `ClosureHandler`'s shape (adds a generic parameter,
   removes a public method, changes a trait bound), every consumer
   of `jmap_sharing_server::ClosureHandler` is broken.

2. **No documentation.** The re-export has no rustdoc explaining
   why it is here, whether it is intended for caller use or only for
   the `register_sharing_handlers` macro internals, or whether it is
   stable. By default, `pub use` items are part of the SemVer
   contract.

3. **Workspace-coordinated release does not relax this.** The
   workspace currently ships `jmap-server` and `jmap-sharing-server`
   together with path deps, but the spec for the published-to-crates.io
   surface is what matters. A consumer that pins
   `jmap-sharing-server = \"0.1\"` and accepts `jmap-server = \"0.2\"`
   in a different transitive path could in principle hit a version
   mismatch on `ClosureHandler`'s identity.

The canonical mail-server has the same re-export at lib.rs:252 — the
divergence here is structural (placement) but the contract risk is
shared across the whole sibling family.

Resolution options (in order of preference):
- Make it `#[doc(hidden)]` if it is purely for the macro internals.
  Mark in rustdoc as \"not stable; do not depend on this path\".
- If it IS intended for caller use, add rustdoc citing the
  workspace's coordinated release policy and stating that the
  upstream `jmap-server` version is implicitly pinned to whatever
  this crate's version pins.
- Remove the re-export and require callers who want `ClosureHandler`
  to depend on `jmap-server` directly. This is the cleanest contract.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: an upstream
breaking change to `ClosureHandler` cascades into a major-version
bump for this crate even though the sharing-server functionality
itself did not change.
notes: Added rustdoc on the ClosureHandler re-export explaining: (a) it exists for the register_sharing_handlers macro body, (b) the re-export pins jmap_server's major-version contract into this crate's surface, (c) consumers SHOULD prefer importing from jmap_server directly for new code. Combined with .9's positional fix.
title: pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler is an undocumented version-pinned cross-crate re-export
